text:
The University of the Andes (Colombia) is a private, non-sectarian university founded in 1949 in Bogotá. It began with 80 students and a small set of faculties, including a College of Superior Studies offering humanities, languages, and social sciences. The university was established with a mission to foster pluralism, diversity, dialogue, and academic excellence, and to provide students with critical and ethical training to address national challenges. It maintains political neutrality and includes representatives from both Conservative and Liberal parties in its governance.
The university's administrative structure includes a Board of Trustees, a Board of Directors, and a Rector (president) who oversees the implementation of the university's development program (PDI). The Academic Council, composed of deans, vice-rectors, and faculty, handles academic and disciplinary matters. The university has 14 academic units, including 10 faculties, and is organized into a system of interdisciplinary studies with a four-cycle academic structure: Basic Professional, Socio-humanistic Electives, Professional, and Professional Complementary cycles.
The campus is located in Bogotá's historical center, an area rich in cultural and institutional landmarks. It is composed of a mixture of renovated industrial and religious buildings and newly constructed facilities, covering 180,551 sq m. The campus includes 116 classrooms, 219 laboratories, a central library, five satellite libraries, and 26 computer rooms, providing over 445,000 books and nearly 2,000 computers for student use. A notable feature is La Caneca, a sports center housing a gym, pool, and courts for various sports.
The university's mascot is a goat named Seneca, inspired by a real goat that roamed the campus in the 1940s and became a symbol of the university. Though the goat no longer lives on campus, Seneca is celebrated annually during Students' Day.
Notable alumni include prominent political figures such as César Gaviria (President of Colombia), María Ángela Holguín (Minister of Foreign Affairs), and Fernando Botero (Minister of National Defense), as well as distinguished professionals in medicine, science, and the arts, including Natalia Castañeda Arbelaez (painter), Ana María Rey (theoretical physicist), and Gabriela Tafur (Miss Colombia).
The university has a strong emphasis on international engagement, offering exchange programs with over 119 universities in 34 countries. It also supports research and innovation through its academic units and has a significant endowment, valued at approximately $426.1 million (COL$1.74 trillion) as of 2020. Its student body is predominantly composed of top high school graduates, with 95% of undergraduates from the top 1% of their national cohort.
